_comment: Fiction prose rules for story/tools/prose_lint.py (STORYMAKER_AUTHORSHIP_PLAN.md QG.1), the same shape as history/lint-rules.json. Data, so a phrase is added by PR with no code change. HARD rules gate an agent's draft: a writer agent runs prose_lint until it exits 0, and a flagged span is repaired, never the whole chapter regenerated. On the AUTHOR's own text every finding is a note: the author's text always wins. Phrase rules run on narration only — text inside double quotation marks is a character speaking, and characters may talk in cliches. Another kind of book brings its own rules file (--rules); nothing in the engine assumes fiction. DECODER SAFETY: comment keys at this TOP LEVEL ONLY.

rules.why: the most-quoted machine cliche in fiction
stock physical reaction; show the specific one
a summary verdict where a detail should be
a decorative abstraction that names nothing
stock; slow the scene with what happens in it
an intrusive narrator spoiling the next scene
stock intensifier
stock paradox
report language in a scene
eyes are eyes
a decorative metaphor; name the sounds or the movements
a word models overuse; people dig, search, read
abstract heaviness instead of a reaction
stock atmosphere
usually removable without loss
a vague turn; say what changed
filler before the action
stock dialogue tag
stock expression
tells the reader what to feel
stock time-stretch
a summary of what the scene should show
a euphemism that hides the action
two named feelings instead of one shown
stock fear
stock focus shift

endings.why: a closing paragraph that explains the scene to the reader; end on the image or the act and let the reader do the understanding

repeats.why: the same six or more words in two places; an editor's repetition note. A deliberate refrain is fine — say so and move on

statScreens.why: status boxes are seasoning: more than two in a chapter, or one longer than ten lines, and the page turns into a spreadsheet. The numbers live in the bible's Stat Changes, where a printed box is checked against them
